title: Domestic obstacles, global opportunities: The road to implementing China’s 15th Five-Year Plan
gist: China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) doubles down on technological self-reliance, supply-chain autonomy and supply-side demand creation, but MERICS argues implementation is constrained by a record CNY 5.89 trillion 2026 deficit, local debt that may exceed GDP, falling fixed asset investment and TFP growth down to 1.7 percent — while Western discord and a record USD 1.2 trillion trade surplus let Beijing keep postponing consumption reform.

themes.theme: 15th FYP priority stack: tech self-reliance over consumption

insights.claim: China's 15th Five-Year Plan, covering 2026-2030, puts economic security, autonomous supply chains, innovation-driven growth, scientific and technological breakthroughs, industrial modernization and a stronger domestic market at the top of the policy agenda.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Capex and subsidy flows through 2030 will keep favouring hard-tech and supply-chain localization over household transfers.
insights.locator: Key findings

insights.claim: Promoting the 'new productive forces' (新质生产力) is Beijing's central policy answer to slowing growth and rising debt, intended to act as an efficiency multiplier across the whole manufacturing sector rather than a narrow sectoral bet.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Read Chinese stimulus as supply-side productivity policy, not demand reflation — a headwind for consumer-facing names, a tailwind for industrial automation.
insights.quote: Promoting the “new productive forces” (新质生产力) has become the leadership’s central response to slowing growth and rising debt.
insights.locator: Boosting industry, innovation and science and technology

insights.claim: Xi Jinping has explicitly framed the new productive forces agenda as upgrading, not abandoning, traditional industries such as steel and textiles, which are expected to absorb smart and AI solutions to lift productivity.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Legacy Chinese heavy industry is a target market for domestic industrial software and automation, not a candidate for orderly shutdown.
insights.locator: Xi Jinping has emphasized that promoting

insights.claim: 'Digital and smart development' receives greater priority in the 15th Five-Year Plan than it did in the 14th, signalling that AI solutions, algorithms and computational models are meant to be embedded into legacy industrial processes.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Industrial AI deployment inside Chinese incumbents is a policy-mandated demand pool through 2030.
insights.locator: “Digital and smart development” is given greater priority

insights.claim: Deepening supply-side structural reform in the plan means cutting overcapacity in specific industrial sectors, avoiding 'ghost projects' and using existing capacity more efficiently rather than adding new lines.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Capacity discipline in overbuilt Chinese sectors would be positive for global industrial pricing — watch whether it is actually enforced.
insights.locator: A central component of this strategy is the deepening

insights.claim: Chinese policy documents can be decoded by four observable signals — chapter placement, section length, changes in phrasing and terminology, and keyword frequency — which together reveal the leadership's true ranking of objectives.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: A repeatable method for pricing Chinese policy: rank priorities by document structure rather than by press-release rhetoric.
insights.locator: Setting priorities and ranking objectives

themes.theme: Supply-induced consumption: demand policy without income transfers

insights.claim: When China's leadership talks about boosting demand it means aggregate demand across the entire value chain, covering intermediate as well as final products, not household consumption alone.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Do not read 'expanding domestic demand' headlines as a consumer-stimulus signal; much of it lands upstream in industrial goods.
insights.locator: Building a Strong Domestic Market

insights.claim: The dual circulation concept, which emerged at a May 2020 Politburo Standing Committee meeting, separates a domestic cycle of production and domestic demand from an international cycle of trade and investment, and elevates the domestic cycle as the main growth driver.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: The doctrinal basis for import substitution: foreign suppliers into China should assume structural share loss regardless of tariff outcomes.
insights.locator: This focus on the domestic market flows from the concept

insights.claim: China's consumption strategy rests on a supply-induced logic — that new and better products will unleash latent demand — with income growth and social benefit expansion included but subordinated to supply-side instruments such as appliance trade-in subsidies.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Consumer recovery bets on China are betting against the actual policy design; subsidy-driven demand pull-forward is the more likely pattern.
insights.quote: Whether latent demand can be activated without significantly boosting underlying household incomes remains to be seen.
insights.locator: China also pursues a strongly supply-oriented approach

insights.claim: Support for households in the plan is concentrated in elder care and childcare expansion plus a promise to link income growth more closely to economic growth, measures likely to stay secondary to supply-side demand stimulus.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Care services are one of the few genuinely policy-favoured consumer verticals in China this cycle.
insights.locator: To support households, the plan provides

themes.theme: Energy transition targets: more renewables, softer carbon intensity

insights.claim: China's plan raises the non-fossil share of total energy consumption from 21.7 percent in 2025 to 25 percent by 2030, backed by large-scale build-outs across all renewable sectors including nuclear power.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: A quantified five-year demand floor for Chinese solar, wind and nuclear supply chains.
insights.locator: Energy policy, green transition, and decarbonization

insights.claim: China lowered its five-year target for reducing CO2 emissions per unit of GDP to 17 percent, down from 18 percent in the 14th Five-Year Plan, after narrowly missing the previous 17.7 percent target.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Beijing is quietly de-rating its own decarbonization pace — bearish for assumptions of aggressive Chinese coal displacement.
insights.locator: However, the target for reducing

insights.claim: Energy security concerns mean China continues to rely on fossil fuels as a backup even while reaffirming decarbonization commitments, and plans to relocate energy-intensive industries to regions with abundant renewable supply.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Chinese coal and gas demand has a policy-sanctioned floor; industrial siting shifts toward western renewable-rich provinces.
insights.locator: While the government continues to reaffirm

themes.theme: Fiscal arithmetic: headline deficit understates the real burden

insights.claim: China set a record projected national general public budget deficit of CNY 5.89 trillion for 2026, six percent above the actual 2025 deficit.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Fiscal expansion continues but from an already stretched base, limiting incremental stimulus capacity.
insights.locator: Budgetary constraints and fiscal pressures

insights.claim: China's 2026 headline deficit target of four percent of GDP excludes CNY 4.4 trillion of special purpose bonds and CNY 1.3 trillion of ultra-long special treasury bonds booked in a separate government funds budget, so the true deficit is materially higher — for comparison France ran 5.1 percent in 2025.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Anyone comparing China's deficit to Western peers on the headline number is understating leverage by several points of GDP.
insights.locator: Still, China’s 2026 headline deficit target

insights.claim: Chinese national debt interest payments have risen by more than half since 2019, consuming five percent of national general public spending in 2025 but almost one fifth of central government spending, and grew over six percent year-on-year in January-April 2026, faster than total expenditure.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Interest crowding out is now visible in the Chinese central budget — each new stimulus round costs more in carry.
insights.locator: Rising budget deficits bring rising national debt

insights.claim: Local governments account for more than 85 percent of China's projected CNY 30 trillion-plus general public budget expenditure and 91 percent of government funds budget spending, while the central government funds under 10 percent of industry spending.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Industrial policy execution risk in China is local-balance-sheet risk; watch provincial finances, not Beijing's headline budget.
insights.locator: Local governments make up the bulk

insights.claim: Officially reported Chinese local government debt stood at CNY 48 trillion in 2024 with LGFV debt estimated at CNY 90-110 trillion, against GDP of CNY 135 trillion, implying total local debt may exceed the size of the economy.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: The single largest hidden liability in the Chinese system; any credible clean-up would absorb years of fiscal space.
insights.quote: local government debt could exceed China’s GDP
insights.locator: Although the extent of the debt remains opaque

insights.claim: As early as 2022, monthly interest costs exceeded monthly revenues in 12 of China's 31 provinces and regions.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: A concrete marker of provincial insolvency risk that predates the current downturn.
insights.locator: Furthermore, as early as 2022

insights.claim: Cash-strapped Chinese local governments have resorted to 'deep-sea fishing' (远洋捕捞) — imposing arbitrary fines on companies to raise revenue — and central rules will not stop the practice while the underlying mismatch between local revenue and spending responsibilities persists.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: A tangible, under-modelled operating-cost and legal risk for companies operating in weak Chinese provinces.
insights.quote: The phrase describes the tactic of imposing arbitrary fines on companies to generate additional funds.
insights.locator: To bolster the public purse

insights.claim: The 15th Five-Year Plan attaches no specific funding amounts to its goals, instead implying a mixed financing model that is part state-directed and part market-based, with capital steered to strategic sectors, more green financing, a selective role for foreign capital and tighter regulation of local investment and debt issuance.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Funding for the plan is contingent, not committed — execution will vary sharply by sector and province.
insights.locator: As a high-level document, the 15th FYP

themes.theme: Cyclical rollover: investment, profits and the R&D squeeze

insights.claim: Fixed asset investment in China fell in 2025 for the first time in decades, returned to negative territory in April 2026 and dropped 4.1 percent in May 2026.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: The investment engine that historically carried Chinese GDP is contracting — commodity and capital-goods demand assumptions need marking down.
insights.locator: Economic momentum is slowing

insights.claim: Chinese growth rose from 4.5 percent in Q4 2025 to 5 percent in Q1 2026 mainly through gross capital formation, but the uptick was policy-induced: state-owned enterprise investment grew 7.1 percent year-on-year and infrastructure investment 8.9 percent.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Treat the Q1 2026 Chinese growth beat as state-directed and unsustainable given local fiscal strain and falling corporate profits.
insights.quote: Yet, most of this uptick appears to be policy-induced
insights.locator: Consequently, stronger gross capital formation

insights.claim: Private-enterprise investment in China declined 8.5 percent in June 2026 and retail sales of consumer goods fell in May for the first time in several years before recovering to just one percent growth in June.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Private-sector confidence, not policy capacity, is the binding constraint on Chinese demand.
insights.locator: At the same time, private business and household confidence

insights.claim: Chinese producer prices turned positive in March 2026 for the first time in over three years and grew 4.1 percent in June, but the move reflected rising oil and raw material input costs rather than stronger end demand.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Do not read China's PPI exit from deflation as a reflation signal — it is a margin squeeze on downstream manufacturers.
insights.quote: still signaled rising input prices rather than stronger demand
insights.locator: In June, producer price growth increased

insights.claim: Persistent overcapacity has driven aggregate operating profits of Chinese industrial enterprises down from a peak of CNY 9.2 trillion in 2021 to CNY 7.2 trillion in 2025, while the share of loss-making industrial firms hit 23.8 percent, almost double the level a decade earlier.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Deteriorating Chinese industrial profitability caps both corporate R&D and the tax base funding state R&D subsidies.
insights.locator: Persisting overcapacity has caused industrial enterprises

insights.claim: Falling corporate profits and growing fiscal pressure together shrink both company-funded and state-subsidized R&D in China, making the plan's technological self-reliance goals harder to reach.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: The financing channel is the real bottleneck for China's tech ambitions — more consequential than export controls in the medium term.
insights.locator: Diminishing profits may restrict the funds

insights.claim: Local protectionism inside China blocks economic integration, so the efficiency gains a genuinely unified domestic market would deliver are never realized.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: The unified national market push is the reform to watch; success would be a genuine productivity upside surprise.
insights.locator: Local protectionism within China hinders

themes.theme: Structural drag: demography, productivity and vanishing startups

insights.claim: China's total factor productivity growth has decayed from an average above four percent per year in 2000-2009 to 2.3 percent in 2010-2019 and just 1.7 percent in 2020-2023, despite a decade of innovation-driven development policy.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: The core evidence that Chinese industrial policy has not yet reproduced the productivity gains urbanization once delivered.
insights.locator: Weak productivity growth is another structural problem

insights.claim: Rapid population aging raises financial pressure on China's pension system while comprehensive social security is still lacking, which is precisely why the government is likely to move cautiously on expanding social benefits.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Demography forecloses the transfer-based consumption boost bulls keep waiting for.
insights.locator: Even more serious are the long-term structural challenges

insights.claim: Youth unemployment in China reached 16.9 percent in March 2026, higher than a year earlier, feeding social discontent and 'lying flat' attitudes that mark a retreat from the traditional meritocracy.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Labour-market stress is now a political variable, raising the odds of ad hoc employment-focused stimulus.
insights.quote: Movements such as “lying flat” (躺平) reflect a shift away from the traditional meritocracy
insights.locator: There is also growing social discontent

insights.claim: New startup formation in China collapsed from 51,302 in 2018 to 1,202 in 2023 and only 260 in the January-August 2024 period, with regulatory intervention and political campaign risk deterring entrepreneurship.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: The innovation pipeline China's plan depends on is thinning at the entry point — a slow-burn negative for future tech leadership.
insights.locator: This societal shift has also dampened startup activity

insights.claim: Keeping and upgrading traditional industries such as steel and textiles for supply-chain security ties up capital that could otherwise flow into emerging sectors and future industries, lowering returns on capital and total factor productivity.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: China's security-first industrial doctrine carries a measurable opportunity cost that will show up in aggregate productivity data.
insights.quote: spending on upgrading traditional industries inevitably ties up resources that could otherwise flow into more lucrative areas
insights.locator: At the same time, China remains committed to modernizing

themes.theme: External environment: discord abroad buys Beijing time

insights.claim: Exports accounted for around 30 percent of China's overall economic growth in 2025 and pushed the trade surplus to a record USD 1.2 trillion, supplying the baseline growth Beijing needs for social stability.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: China's growth is more externally dependent than the domestic-demand rhetoric implies, making tariff escalation a first-order macro risk.
insights.quote: In 2025, exports accounted for around 30 percent of overall economic growth, pushing China’s trade surplus to a record USD 1.2 trillion.
insights.locator: China has been able to rely on exports

insights.claim: China still enjoys continued access to foreign technologies it needs, including high-purity silicon and electronic design automation software in the semiconductor supply chain.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: EDA and specialty materials remain the live chokepoints — any tightening there bites harder than finished-chip controls.
insights.locator: China can still depend on continued access

insights.claim: The EU is developing economic security rules that would force European companies to source critical components such as chemicals and machinery from at least three suppliers not all based in one country, while Macron has pushed for Section 301-style anti-dumping and anti-monopoly tools and even Germany has signalled willingness to back stricter measures.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: European supply-chain diversification mandates would redirect chemicals and machinery procurement away from China — a multi-year order-book shift.
insights.locator: This diligence in execution takes place against the backdrop

insights.claim: The May 2026 summit between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping extended the China-US trade truce, while EU-China relations moved into rockier territory before both sides reengaged in trade talks.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: US-China trade risk is temporarily capped; the marginal escalation risk has rotated to Europe.
insights.locator: The May summit between Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping

insights.claim: International uncertainty and discord — inconsistent US policy under Trump and EU member state hesitation on economic security tools — give Beijing room to maneuver and stick to its own course.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Western policy incoherence is itself a support for Chinese assets; coordinated Western action is the tail risk to hedge.
insights.quote: The international situation is characterized by uncertainty and discord, which gives China room to maneuver.
insights.locator: Outlook: Despite obstacles

insights.claim: The very factors currently favouring Beijing are a double-edged sword, because short-term breathing space encourages further delay of the income expansion, redistribution and consumption reforms needed to shift from export-led to consumption-driven growth.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Expect the consumption rebalancing story to keep slipping; position for a China that stays an export and capex economy.
insights.locator: However, these favorable factors could be a double-edged sword

insights.claim: China's reliance on exports as a growth pillar could break if EU-China trade talks fail and the EU finds the stomach for tougher measures.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: EU trade-instrument decisions are the key catalyst to monitor for Chinese export-linked equities and industrial commodities.
insights.locator: Although China has long been able to rely on exports
